epics.description: Customers can export their paid orders as a CSV file from their account page. Each paid order is one row with its order number, date and total amount including VAT. Cancelled orders are excluded. The file name is orders-YYYY-MM-DD.csv, where the date is the export date in Europe/Paris. The delimiter and encoding follow the project's CSV export standard: UTF-8 without BOM, semicolon-delimited, with a header row.

features.description: Customer capability to download their paid orders as a CSV file from the account page.
features.name: Order export

acceptanceCriteria: Given a logged-in customer on the account page, When they trigger the export, Then a CSV file is downloaded.
Given an export triggered on a given day, When the file is downloaded, Then its name is orders-YYYY-MM-DD.csv with the export date in Europe/Paris.
Given a customer with paid orders and orders of other customers, When they export, Then the file contains only their own paid orders.
stories.aiReadyReason: The story defines the trigger, the paid-order scope (matching the glossary), the file name rule using the Europe/Paris export date, and the per-customer isolation, so a developer can implement it and verify each criterion.
stories.description: A download action on the customer account page exports the logged-in customer's paid orders as a CSV file. A paid order is one whose payment is captured and which is not fully refunded. The file name is orders-YYYY-MM-DD.csv, where the date is the export date in the Europe/Paris timezone.
stories.iWant: to download my paid orders as a CSV file from my account page
stories.soThat: I can keep and analyse my order history outside the shop

tasks.description: Add a backend data access method that returns only the orders of the authenticated customer that are paid, meaning payment captured and not fully refunded, and excludes cancelled orders and orders of other customers. Expected result: the query returns only that customer's paid orders.
tasks.title: Implement paid orders query for the logged-in customer

tasks.description: Add a backend endpoint that accepts an export request from a logged-in customer, uses the paid orders query, and returns a file download response. The file name is orders-YYYY-MM-DD.csv, where the date is the current date in the Europe/Paris timezone. Expected result: an authenticated customer receives a CSV attachment with the correct name, and an unauthenticated request is rejected.
tasks.title: Implement authenticated export endpoint for paid orders CSV

tasks.description: Add a download action on the customer account page in the React frontend that calls the export endpoint and saves the returned CSV file. Expected result: a logged-in customer on the account page can trigger the export and the browser downloads the file.
tasks.title: Add download action on the account page

tasks.description: Write automated tests that verify a download is produced for a logged-in customer, the file name uses the Europe/Paris export date, and the file contains only that customer's paid orders and not orders of other customers or unpaid and cancelled orders. Expected result: all three acceptance criteria pass.
tasks.title: Test paid orders export acceptance criteria

stories.title: Download paid orders CSV from account page

acceptanceCriteria: Given a customer with three paid orders and one cancelled order, When they export, Then the file has exactly three data rows, one per paid order.
Given a paid order, When it is exported, Then its row contains its order number and its total amount including VAT.
Given a cancelled order, When the customer exports, Then this order does not appear in the file.
Given an order that is fully refunded, When the customer exports, Then this order does not appear in the file.
stories.aiReadyReason: The description states that the meaning of the date column is undefined and must be decided before implementation, so the story is blocked: Which date should the date column contain (order placement date or another date)?
dependencies: Download paid orders CSV from account page
stories.description: The exported file contains exactly one data row per paid order, excluding cancelled orders and fully refunded orders. Each row holds the order number, a date and the total amount including VAT. The specification does not define which date the date column contains (for example the order placement date or another date), so this must be decided before implementation.
stories.iWant: each paid order to appear as one row with its order number, date and total amount including VAT
stories.soThat: I can see the key figures of each order in the export
stories.title: Export one row per paid order with key order data

acceptanceCriteria: Given any order export, When the file is saved, Then it is encoded in UTF-8 without BOM.
Given any order export, When the file is read, Then its fields are separated by semicolons and its first row is a header row.
Given an exported order with a date and a total amount, When the file is read, Then the date is written as YYYY-MM-DD and the amount uses a dot with exactly two decimals.
stories.aiReadyReason: The UTF-8 without BOM, semicolon, header row, YYYY-MM-DD and two-decimal dot formats are all defined by the project's CSV export standard in the context, and the header names are explicitly left to the developer, so every criterion is verifiable.
dependencies: Export one row per paid order with key order data
stories.description: The project's CSV export standard applies to the order export: UTF-8 without BOM, semicolon as delimiter, a header row, dates in YYYY-MM-DD format and amounts with a dot as decimal separator and exactly two decimals. This resolves the open question on delimiter and encoding in the specification. The header column names are left to the developer.
stories.iWant: the export file to be UTF-8 without BOM, semicolon-delimited, with a header row, dates as YYYY-MM-DD and amounts with a dot and two decimals
stories.soThat: the file is consistent with the other CSV exports of the application

tasks.description: Implement in the backend order export writer the project CSV standard: UTF-8 encoding without BOM, semicolon as delimiter, and a first header row whose column names are chosen by the developer. Expected result: any order export is saved as UTF-8 without BOM with semicolon-separated fields and a header row.
tasks.title: Apply UTF-8 semicolon CSV format to order export writer

tasks.description: Implement in the backend order export the formatting of dates as YYYY-MM-DD and amounts with a dot as decimal separator and exactly two decimals. Expected result: an exported order date reads as YYYY-MM-DD and an exported total amount such as 12.5 reads as 12.50.
tasks.title: Format dates and amounts in order export

tasks.description: Write automated tests that read a generated order export and verify UTF-8 without BOM encoding, semicolon delimiters, a header row, YYYY-MM-DD dates and two-decimal dot-separated amounts. Expected result: all three acceptance criteria pass.
tasks.title: Test CSV export format acceptance criteria

stories.title: Format export file as UTF-8 semicolon CSV with header
